findings.consequence: A failed run can retain stale or absent whole_child_resources, omit final elapsed/RSS/CUDA maxima and omit terminal cap-exceedance status. A cleanup/source-check exception can also prevent recording separate restoration errors and can replace the original failure. This finding concerns failure evidence; it does not establish that the existing successful PASS path bypasses its final limits() check.
findings.evidence: At line557 resources() returns a fresh snapshot but the return is discarded. The limits() at line559 is reached only when the try/finally completes successfully; exception paths skip it. The straight-line environment/signal/source/gate restoration checks at lines545–555 can also throw before terminal bookkeeping at line557. The outer main failure handler saves a FAIL receipt, but does not take a final resource snapshot.
findings.remaining_after_remedy: A separately supervised run must still establish terminal closure, whole-child resource compliance and actual restoration.
findings.smallest_remedy: Use unconditional finalization around cleanup. Store the fresh resources() row into receipt[whole_child_resources] and record each observed value against the existing cap, including exceedances. Ensure this bookkeeping runs even when a restoration/source check raises. Preserve the original primary failure and record restoration and resource-collection errors independently. Preserve successful limits() enforcement; any original, restoration, collection or cap failure must remain a failure.
findings.title: Persist terminal resources and cap status on every failure and restoration path
